_about: Health conditions, age groups, travel modes and kinds of work for the profile form. Thresholds and tips are our own public-health heuristics, not medical advice.

asthma.label: Asthma
asthma.why: Fine particles inflame airways that are already sensitive, so attacks come sooner and harder.
asthma.tip: Keep your reliever inhaler with you and use your preventer as prescribed.
asthma.watch: Cough, wheeze, a tight chest, or needing your reliever more than usual.

copd.label: COPD or emphysema
copd.why: Damaged lungs have less reserve, so a bad-air day can tip you into a flare-up.
copd.tip: Keep outdoor time short and follow your COPD action plan.
copd.watch: Breathlessness worse than usual, more or darker phlegm.

bronchitis.label: Chronic bronchitis or frequent chest infections
bronchitis.why: Pollution irritates the airways and makes chest infections more likely.
bronchitis.tip: Steam inhalation and warm fluids help clear mucus; avoid smoke of any kind.
bronchitis.watch: A cough that keeps getting worse, fever, or green or bloody phlegm.

tb.label: TB, now or in the past
tb.why: TB can leave scarring that makes the lungs react more to polluted air.
tb.tip: Finish any TB treatment fully and keep follow-up visits, even on bad-air days.
tb.watch: Cough for more than two weeks, coughing blood, night sweats or weight loss.

covid.label: Recent COVID or long COVID
covid.why: Lungs that are still recovering are easily irritated, and breathlessness can return.
covid.tip: Build activity up slowly and do it indoors on poor-air days.
covid.watch: Breathlessness at rest, chest pain, or a racing heart.

allergic_rhinitis.label: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever) or dust allergy
allergic_rhinitis.why: Dust and smoke set off sneezing, a blocked nose and itching, and can trigger asthma in some people.
allergic_rhinitis.tip: Rinse your nose with saline after being out, and take your allergy medicine as prescribed.
allergic_rhinitis.watch: Wheeze or a tight chest along with your usual allergy symptoms.

sinusitis.label: Sinusitis
sinusitis.why: Polluted air dries and inflames the sinuses, so blocked, painful sinuses last longer.
sinusitis.tip: Saline nose rinses and steam help; drink plenty of water.
sinusitis.watch: Facial pain with fever, or symptoms lasting more than ten days.

eyes.label: Eye irritation, dry eyes or conjunctivitis
eyes.why: Smoke and dust make eyes red, watery and itchy.
eyes.tip: Wear glasses or sunglasses outdoors, wash your eyes with clean water after, and do not rub them.
eyes.watch: Eye pain, blurred vision or a lot of discharge.

heart.label: Heart disease or high blood pressure
heart.why: Fine particles get into the blood, raise blood pressure and make the heart work harder.
heart.tip: Avoid hard effort outdoors and keep taking your heart and BP medicines.
heart.watch: Chest pain or pressure, palpitations, or unusual breathlessness.

stroke.label: Had a stroke or mini-stroke
stroke.why: Polluted air thickens the blood and raises the risk of another stroke.
stroke.tip: Keep taking your blood thinners and BP medicines, and avoid outdoor effort on bad days.
stroke.watch: Sudden weakness on one side, a drooping face, slurred speech: call 112 at once.

anaemia.label: Anaemia
anaemia.why: With less oxygen in the blood, the heart and lungs already work harder, and polluted air adds to that.
anaemia.tip: Take iron or other supplements as prescribed and keep outdoor effort light.
anaemia.watch: Dizziness, a pounding heart or breathlessness on light effort.

diabetes.label: Diabetes
diabetes.why: Polluted air raises inflammation and can make blood sugar harder to control.
diabetes.tip: Keep exercise going but move it indoors on poor-air days, and check your sugar as usual.
diabetes.watch: Feeling unwell with high or unusually low sugar readings.

kidney.label: Kidney disease
kidney.why: Kidney disease often comes with heart strain, which polluted air makes worse.
kidney.tip: Keep outdoor effort light and follow your fluid advice.
kidney.watch: Swelling, breathlessness or much less urine.

immune.label: Weak immunity (cancer treatment, transplant, HIV, steroids)
immune.why: A weaker immune system means polluted air is more likely to lead to chest infections.
immune.tip: Wear an N95 in crowded or smoky places and avoid people with colds.
immune.watch: Fever, a new cough or breathlessness: call your doctor early.

pregnant.label: Pregnant
pregnant.why: Polluted air is linked to low birth weight and early birth, and you breathe more air while pregnant.
pregnant.tip: Prefer indoor exercise on poor-air days and keep windows shut at the worst hours.
pregnant.watch: Breathlessness, a bad headache, or less movement from the baby: see your doctor.

smoker.label: I smoke or vape
smoker.why: Smoke already irritates your lungs, and outdoor pollution adds to the same damage.
smoker.tip: Bad-air days are a good time to cut down; do not smoke indoors, where it adds to the air everyone breathes.
smoker.watch: A cough that will not go away, or getting breathless sooner than before.

child.why: Children breathe faster for their size and their lungs are still growing, so they take in more pollution.
child.tip: Move play and sport indoors when the air is poor, and keep the school run off main roads.
child.watch: Coughing at night, wheeze, or getting breathless at play.

older.why: After 60 the lungs and heart react sooner to polluted air.
older.tip: Walk at the cleanest hour, keep it gentle, and keep your usual medicines close.
older.watch: Breathlessness, chest discomfort, dizziness or unusual tiredness.

commute_tips.walk: Walk on side streets away from heavy traffic where you can.
commute_tips.cycle: Cycle on quieter roads, and a well-fitted N95 helps on busy ones.
commute_tips.two_wheeler: A well-fitted N95 under the helmet cuts what you breathe in traffic.
commute_tips.auto: Autos are open to traffic fumes; an N95 helps on long rides.
commute_tips.bus: Wait for the bus away from the kerb when you can.
commute_tips.metro: The metro is one of the cleaner ways to travel; keep the walk to the station short.
commute_tips.car: Keep windows up and the air on recirculate in heavy traffic.

vehicle_labels.help: The BS level is on the registration certificate (RC). It decides which GRAP vehicle rules apply to you.
